objective: Define capital-budgeting/project-economics semantics for stock-selection research without duplicating management-allocation governance evidence.
corePrinciple: Project economics and management allocation quality are different layers. D07-19 owns ex-ante project cash-flow economics and flexibility value; D21-07 owns managerial incentives, approval/process quality and realized allocation behavior.

projectEconomics.primaryDecisionMetric: NPV is the primary value-additivity metric when project cash flows and a risk-consistent discount rate are specified.
projectEconomics.irrRole: IRR is descriptive/supportive only. It can mis-rank mutually exclusive projects, produce multiple/no solutions for non-conventional cash flows, and embeds reinvestment/scale assumptions that can conflict with value maximization.
projectEconomics.mirrRole: MIRR may be used as a diagnostic when reinvestment assumptions matter, but it does not replace NPV as the value-additivity anchor.
cashFlowRules: Use incremental after-tax cash flows attributable to the project.
Exclude sunk costs already incurred before the decision clock.
Include opportunity costs of resources consumed by the project.
Include cannibalization and cross-project spillovers when economically attributable.
Keep financing cash flows out of operating project cash flow when discounting FCFF at WACC; do not double-count financing effects in both cash flow and discount rate.
Match nominal cash flows with nominal discount rates and real cash flows with real discount rates.
Terminal value assumptions must have explicit horizon, reinvestment and competitive-fade logic rather than perpetual extrapolation by default.
mutuallyExclusiveProjects: When projects are mutually exclusive, compare incremental cash-flow NPV under a common decision date and consistent risk treatment.
Do not choose the highest IRR when scale or timing differences cause NPV disagreement.

realOptions.admissionRule: Real-option value is admitted only when management has an actual decision right, uncertainty resolves over time, and the right can change future cash flows or commitment. Narrative flexibility without a concrete decision right is not an option.
doubleCountGuard: Do not add a generic real-option premium on top of forecast cash flows that already embed the same expansion/abandonment scenario.
Do not count market volatility as option value unless the uncertainty maps to project cash-flow dispersion and a valid decision right.
Do not treat strategic optimism, TAM size or management optionality language as measured option value without observable exercise states.

pitContract.asOfRule: All opportunity-set, project-cost, demand, price, volume, margin, capacity, tax, discount-rate and timing assumptions must have knownAt <= projectDecisionKnownAt.
pitContract.revisionRule: Later guidance, cost overruns, utilization, margins, impairments or realized returns are appended as later vintages and may be outcomes; they may not rewrite the original ex-ante project state.
pitContract.unknownRule: Missing project-specific assumptions remain UNKNOWN. Do not infer NPV/IRR from later realized capex or from management adjectives.

D07_19: opportunity cost, sunk cost and cannibalization treatment
ownershipBoundary.D07_18: Owns enterprise WACC/cost-of-capital composite; D07-19 consumes a fit-for-project discount rate but does not independently recreate macro/risk-free/debt-cost inputs as separate alpha votes.
ownershipBoundary.D07_20_D07_23: Three-statement, driver and scenario forecasting modules may supply project assumptions; D07-19 owns the investment-decision transformation, not duplicate forecasts.
ownershipBoundary.D08: Valuation modules may use project economics as an input to firm value but must not create a second independent project-quality vote from the same forecast cash flows.

divergentStates.description: Positive project NPVs can coexist with poor managerial sequencing, financing, empire-building or overcommitment. D07-19 may be positive while D21-07 is negative.
Management can display disciplined governance by rejecting weak projects or returning capital. D07-19 opportunity-set state can be weak while D21-07 is positive.
A small project can show a high IRR but create less absolute value than a larger lower-IRR project; mutually exclusive choice follows NPV.
A staged/deferable project can have negative static NPV yet positive expanded NPV if a real, exercisable flexibility right is economically material and not double-counted.

falsification: Reject a universal high-IRR-is-better rule if project rankings reverse under NPV because of scale/timing.
Reject a universal capex-growth-is-good rule; capex amount alone does not establish positive NPV.
Reject inferred project quality when the opportunity set and project assumptions are not observable at decision time.
Reject real-option claims when no concrete exercise right, uncertainty-resolution path or decision boundary is observable.
Mark REDUNDANT if D07-19-derived state adds no information beyond D07-18 cost of capital, D07-20/21 forecasts, D21-07 allocation behavior and D08 valuation controls.
Do not promote if effects are concentrated in one industry, one mega-cap issuer, one capex cycle or one narrative-heavy disclosure regime.
Do not promote if later realized utilization/margins are needed to reconstruct the original project economics.
researchHypotheses: H1: Explicit project-economics quality may improve downside/MAE or false-growth filtering beyond raw capex growth.
H2: NPV-consistent opportunity-set quality may add more to long-horizon selection than short-horizon D1/D3 returns.
H3: Staged/defer/abandon flexibility should matter more in high-uncertainty, high-irreversibility industries than in routine replacement capex.
H4: Poor project economics and poor management allocation are correlated but not identical; incremental tests must residualize one against the other.
H5: Project-economics evidence may be most useful as context/validation rather than a standalone stock-selection score.
taiwanSourceFeasibilityPlan: MOPS/TWSE material information for board-approved capex, acquisitions/disposals and major capacity projects where amount/purpose/timing are disclosed.
Issuer annual reports and financial reports for cash-flow statements, PPE additions, commitments, segment/capacity notes and later impairment/utilization context.
Issuer investor-conference materials for contemporaneous project assumptions only when publication timestamp is preserved.
D07-18 cost-of-capital receipts for risk-consistent discount-rate inputs.
Prospective observer should preserve original disclosure payload/hash and later revisions append-only.

maturityDecision.rationale: Mechanism, ownership boundary, falsification, PIT semantics and divergent states are now explicitly defined. Taiwan project-level replay is not yet physically validated, so L3 remains closed.

l3Gate: At least two Taiwan-listed issuers from materially different industries.
Historically replayable project decision disclosures with original knownAt/firstObservedAt.
At least one project with later revision/cost-overrun/utilization or cancellation path to prove append-only vintage handling.
A case where project economics and D21-07 governance/allocation state diverge.
Project-specific discount-rate assumption or a documented fail-closed UNKNOWN when unavailable.
No outcome leakage from later operating results into decision-time project state.
l4Gate: Controls for size, industry, growth, leverage, valuation, regime and pre-existing trend/RS.
Independent dates and multiple project families.
Incrementality versus capex growth, ROIC, WACC and D21-07 allocation-quality features.
